sentence: Unintentional weight loss means losing weight without changing diet or exercise, and the NHS advises seeing a GP as a precaution.
The NHS lists mental health conditions, digestive problems, overactive thyroid and heart failure among the causes.
A GP will ask about general health and may arrange tests or scans.
Unintentional weight loss is losing weight without changing your diet or exercise routine.
The NHS treats it as a possible sign of stress or serious illness, and advises seeing a GP as a precaution.
Mental health conditions such as depression, anxiety, eating disorders and obsessive compulsive disorder (OCD) are on the NHS list.
Digestive problems are listed, including coeliac disease and inflammatory bowel disease.
Hormone conditions such as an overactive thyroid and type 1 diabetes can cause weight loss.
Heart conditions such as heart failure are also listed.
Some medicines can cause weight loss as well, and cancer is another possible cause.
The NHS advises seeing a GP if you keep losing weight without changing your diet or exercise.
The NHS says to go as soon as possible if the weight loss comes with other symptoms.
NHS malnutrition advice also says to see a GP after losing a lot of weight unintentionally over a few months.

sentence: A GP will ask about general health and may arrange some tests or scans.
Blood tests commonly used in the first assessment can include a full blood count, liver and kidney function, thyroid function and a test for diabetes.
